source_resources.title: Python Data Model & Mutability Reference
source_resources.author: Python Software Foundation
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under PSF open documentation terms; no proprietary content imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic command line and high school reading comprehension
source_resources.selection_rationale: Normative reference on Python identity vs value semantics and mutable vs immutable types without tutorial inaccuracies.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Standard documentation hosted on python.org; accessible worldwide with offline standard library documentation bundle as local fallback.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Official documentation is mirrored locally via standard library pydoc and embedded offline lesson explanations if internet access is interrupted.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: High pedagogical clarity for Python fundamentals, but structures mutability around academic lecture pacing rather than immediate hands-on minimal reproductions (MRE).

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch (Spring 2024)
compared_candidates.license: No license declared (the repository has no LICENSE file, so all rights are reserved by default)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong systems engineering and PyTorch tensor rigor, but assumes advanced Python mastery and PyTorch installed; deferred to Days 30-60 model pretraining.

compared_candidates.license: 3Blue1Brown copyright (all rights reserved); site FAQ permits only short clips under stated conditions
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong visual intuition for linear transformations and vector spaces; selected for Days 10-18 mathematics foundations, but not relevant for Day 01 Python object references.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero (micrograd)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Clear, executable autograd intuition; code is MIT license, but video subtitles have unknown/proprietary distribution rights (prohibiting full-text transcript import). Selected for Days 19-25 autograd implementation with linking-only reuse.

source_resources.title: The Python Tutorial: Virtual Environments and Packages
source_resources.author: Python Software Foundation
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 12 (creating venvs, pip installs, requirements files)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under PSF open documentation terms; no source text imported into curriculum content.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic Python syntax from Study Days 01-09
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary reference for python -m venv and interpreter isolation, which the Day 01 drill checks through activation, the sys.prefix/sys.base_prefix probes, and python -m pip --version; its requirements-file and wrong-environment material is practiced later, on Study Day 11.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on python.org; pip installs additionally need a reachable package index.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The Day 01 drill needs no network: venv creation and activation, the sys.executable/sys.prefix/sys.base_prefix probes, the venv interpreter's marker.txt read, python -m pip --version, and deactivate all run offline; without a supported Python, the exercise's recorded no-interpreter fallback applies.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Primary reference for pip commands, but the tutorial presents the create-activate-install loop as one beginner-friendly narrative.
Mature third-party environment tool with overlapping behavior; the stdlib venv tutorial was selected to avoid an extra dependency for first-time setup.

source_resources.title: Python Standard Library: pathlib
source_resources.author: Python Software Foundation
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Path.exists, Path.cwd, and anchoring paths to __file__
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under PSF open documentation terms; no source text imported into curriculum content.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic Python syntax from Study Days 01-09
source_resources.selection_rationale: Background reference for working-directory-relative file access: the Day 01 drill's venv interpreter reads marker.txt from the current directory using open(), not pathlib; Path.exists()/Path.cwd() evidence that separates an absent file from a wrong working directory is practiced on Study Day 10.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Hosted on python.org; requires internet access unless a local documentation bundle is installed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Not needed to complete the Day 01 drill, which makes no pathlib call, so no online page is required; Path.exists() and Path.cwd() are exercised offline on Study Day 10.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Functionally equivalent for exists() checks; pathlib keeps the beginner syntax object-oriented and consistent across the block.
Covers copying and moving whole trees rather than path modeling; pathlib remains the right reference for the filesystem checks these days rehearse.

source_resources.title: Pro Git, Second Edition
source_resources.author: Scott Chacon and Ben Straub
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Chapter 3 (Git Branching), Section 7.7 (Reset Demystified), Sections 5.2/6.2 (Contributing to a Project)
source_resources.permission_basis: Linking only; no book text reproduced in curriculum content; reuse limited to noncommercial references consistent with CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic git status/log/diff vocabulary from earlier study days
source_resources.selection_rationale: Freely licensed reference for branching, merging, conflict resolution, and safe recovery vocabulary used on Day 14.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Readable free at git-scm.com; availability depends on the site staying online.
source_resources.safe_fallback: git help <command> and the Git manual pages ship with Git and cover the same commands offline; every required workflow is stated locally in the lesson.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Interactive but requires a GitHub account and an external service; disposable local repositories keep the exercise self-contained.
Vendor-owned prose with no permissive license; Pro Git covers the same ground under CC BY-NC-SA.

source_resources.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention
source_resources.author: Henry L. Roediger III, Jeffrey D. Karpicke
source_resources.license: Journal publisher copyright (all rights reserved) - lawful external linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external citation of the publisher record; no text imported into curriculum materials.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic understanding of study sessions, retention intervals, and experimental design vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational experimental evidence that retrieval practice (testing) outperforms repeated study for long-term retention; grounds the Day 88 AI-free retrieval checks in peer-reviewed learning science rather than folk advice.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publisher page may be paywalled; author preprints and university repositories host lawful copies.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum restates the experimental design and effect sizes in original prose; every sealed task runs without the paper.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Cepeda et al. Distributed Practice in Verbal Recall Tasks: A Review and Quantitative Synthesis
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong meta-analytic coverage of spacing effects but addresses scheduling rather than the retrieval effect itself; retained as support for the Day 90 spaced-review schedule.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Karpicke & Roediger: The Critical Importance of Retrieval for Learning (Science 2008)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Equally foundational follow-up demonstrating repeated retrieval vs repeated study; the 2006 paper is cited as the standard first controlled demonstration.

source_resources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology
source_resources.author: John Dunlosky, Katherine A. Rawson, Elizabeth J. Marsh, Mitchell J. Nathan, Daniel T. Willingham
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1): 4-58; practice testing and distributed practice sections
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 2013 (Verified: 2026-10-30)
source_resources.license: Journal publisher copyright (all rights reserved) - lawful external linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external citation of the publisher record; no text imported into curriculum materials.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Detailed comparative review rating practice testing and distributed practice as high-utility techniques while rating highlighting and rereading low-utility; anchors the retrieval, correction, and spaced-review design of Days 88-90.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Paywalled at SAGE; author-hosted preprints exist on university sites.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Curriculum restates the utility ratings and application conditions in original prose; every task remains runnable offline.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Pashler et al. Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
compared_candidates.license: Publisher copyright (originally Wiley; now SAGE Publications)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Important negative result on learning-styles matching but narrower scope; Dunlosky et al. rates a broader set of techniques directly usable for this curriculum.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Brown, Roediger & McDaniel: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Strong trade-book synthesis of the same evidence base; the peer-reviewed review is preferred for citation precision and technique-by-technique utility ratings.
